newsitem.title: USA: Farm Credit System Q4 net $250 mln vs $258 mln.
newsitem.headline: Farm Credit System Q4 net $250 mln vs $258 mln.

text.p: The Federal Farm Credit Banks Funding Corp said Tuesday it earned $250 million in the fourth quarter of 1996, down from $258 million in the year-earlier period.
For all of 1996, the Farm Credit System earned $1.201 billion, compared with $1.165 billion in 1995.

Nonperforming assets totaled $974 million at the end of 1996, down from $1.213 billion a year earlier. Such assets, said the Farm Credit System, represented 1.6 percent of all loans and property owned, versus 2.1 percent a year earlier.
The decline in nonperforming assets was attributable, said the lenders, to the relatively high levels of net farm cash income over the past several years.

The US Department of Agriculture said, however, that this income, at a near-record level in 1996, was likely to decline in 1997. The USDA also said that while farm debt levels will continue to rise moderatley this year, borrowers have an improved chance of withstandng any future adversity because of favorable income levels over the past years.
The Farm Credit System is a nationwide system of federally-chartered agricultural lending institutions cooperatively owned by their borrowers.
